articles.title: Anodized Hex Fade
articles.summary: Hexagonal panels with polished raised lips and a soft electric fade across the surface. A faint honeycomb web in the lit zone; at distance it reads as a smooth anodised sheen with a slight geometric shimmer.
articles.what: Anodized hex panels with electric fade and polished cell lips. Up close: A fine triangular or hex lattice of thin bright lines about 45 px apart, drawn as polished cell lips with soft flat panels between them. On metal the web of lines is crisp inside the highlight band; on satin it is a faint ghost grid. From a distance: A faint honeycomb web in the lit zone; at distance it reads as a smooth anodised sheen with a slight geometric shimmer. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Anodized Hex Fade".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on a metallic base where the lattice can read
Spoiler and splitter for a machined feel
Numbers stay clean; lines are thin and faint enough not to interfere.
Very faint: a ghost web of lines only inside the brightest zone
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a coloured anodise: no rainbow or hue, only shine lines
Not Anodized Texture: this has a visible lattice, not smooth sand grain
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Anodized Hex Fade over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Circuit Solder Mask
articles.summary: Faint micro-grain sheen, near-flat gloss with sparse tiny bright flecks; reads almost clean. Gone at distance; at most a faint grid-like sheen in the hot highlight.
articles.what: PCB traces, solder pads, via rings, and gloss mask islands. Up close: Hair-thin bright lines running at right angles in a loose lattice, with tiny dots at some crossings, like PCB traces and vias. The lines are 1-2 px wide with cells of 25-60 px; clear on metallic, a whisper on satin. From a distance: Gone at distance; at most a faint grid-like sheen in the hot highlight. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). articles.title: Guilloche Watch Dial
articles.summary: Very fine watch-dial guilloche waves; subtle jeweled cuts, low coverage, delicate shimmer. Reads as a smooth sheen with a very fine, slightly silky grain; no engraving pattern is visible from any distance.
articles.what: Fine watch-dial guilloche waves and jeweled engraved cuts. Up close: Extremely fine texture: tiny horizontal-ish dashes and dots, a few pixels long, packed densely like micro engraving or dust. The wave lines of a real guilloche dial are too fine to resolve at 1:1; you see a grainy glitter inside the highlight. From a distance: Reads as a smooth sheen with a very fine, slightly silky grain; no engraving pattern is visible from any distance. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: trim, numbers, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Guilloche Watch Dial".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.

Hood and roof on metallic bases for best effect
Numbers keep their colour; the micro grain does not touch legibility.

pitfalls: Not a visible watch-dial design: no concentric waves are resolvable
Not brushed metal: dashes are short and scattered, not long hairlines
Avoid: lost on matte, too subtle for body.

articles.title: Laser Etched Microbar
articles.summary: Barely-there satin micro bars and tick marks, almost uniform sheen with faint burn streaks. Reads as a clean smooth sheen with no visible pattern.
articles.what: Laser-etched micro bars, registration ticks, and satin burn marks. Up close: Nearly smooth with a very faint regular stipple of tiny dots about 10 px apart, visible only in the highlight on metal. The micro bars and registration ticks in the description are not readable at 1:1. From a distance: Reads as a clean smooth sheen with no visible pattern. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, roof, under stripes.
